name: Electric carving knife
description: A corded kitchen knife with two serrated blades that saw against each other when it runs. Needs mains power.
notes: Modelled switched off; the reference's running state would share this model. No tool quality: the reference gives none while off, and a powered cutting quality needs power handling the drafts cannot express. The cord is a short stub with its plug so the length matches the reference's 482 mm; box volume 1.33 times the reference because the handle is round.

name: Charcoal water filter
description: A gravity filter: water poured in the top runs down through cloth, charcoal, sand and gravel and out of the tap. The charcoal wears out with use.
notes: The layers are drawn as bands on the outside of a white frame so they read from the iso view; the reservoir is clear blue and the tile draws it opaque. No tool quality: purifying water is a use action on a container, which has no draft field yet. Box volume 1.6 times the reference, as a cylinder in its bounding box.

name: Charcoal smoker
description: A portable bullet smoker on three legs, with a fuel door at the front and a domed lid. Burns charcoal; coal fumes would spoil the meat.
notes: heating stands for the reference's hotplate quality. 300 mm across and 600 mm tall to the lid handle, a small real smoker's size; its box volume is 3.7 times the reference's 20 L, which is low for any bullet smoker, so the shape follows the real thing. Default grain, as it is larger than a shoebox.

name: Charcoal cooker
description: A small steel firebox for coal or charcoal with a pot grate on top, a pilot valve to light it and a flue to carry the fumes away.
notes: The 300 mm longest side is the flue, which rises behind the tank; box volume is 3.9 times the reference because the flue stands off the tank. heating stands for the reference's hotplate quality.

name: Clay pot
description: A rough hand-built cooking pot of fired clay, open at the top, with two lugs to lift it by.
notes: Qualities follow the reference, under the names other batches use. Box volume 3 times the reference's 2.1 L, which is the capacity rather than the outside of a round pot with lugs.

name: Clay teapot
description: A round fired-clay teapot with a lid, a spout and a loop handle.
notes: CHECK VOLUME: the box is 5.2 times the reference's 0.79 L, which is the pot's capacity; the spout and handle stand well out from a round body, so its bounding box is mostly air.

name: Coffeemaker
description: A drip coffeemaker: water heats in the back tower and drips through the filter basket into a glass carafe on a warming plate. Needs power.
notes: The carafe holds a little coffee, which shows only in game; the tile draws the glass opaque. Qualities follow the reference.

name: Crystallizing sugar
description: A small glass of thick sugar syrup with a skewer pegged across the rim, crystals slowly growing on it. Takes about two weeks to set.
notes: CHECK MASS VOLUME: the reference's 10 g and 10 ml are the sugar alone; the model is the glass a player would pick up, so its mass is 80 g with the glass and the box is far larger. The crystals sit below the rim and show only in game, where the glass is see-through.

name: Food dehydrator
description: A round electric dryer with five stacked trays over a fan and heater base, for drying food to keep. Needs power.
notes: Trays are amber plastic so the stack reads against the white base and lid. No tool quality: the reference gives none, and drying food is a use action. Box volume 1.6 times the reference, a cylinder in its bounding box.

name: Jar of pickling eggs
description: An open glass jar of peeled eggs in brine, still pickling. Seal it once they are done.
notes: Left open, as the reference is sealed only when the process ends; the sealed jar would need its own model with a lid. The whole jar is one item, so the mass includes the glass. The eggs show only through the mouth in the tile, which draws the glass opaque; the brine uses syrup-green for want of a pale pickling-brine finish.

name: Hexamine stove
description: A pocket-sized folding stove that burns solid fuel tablets. Opened out, its two side walls hold up a small pot.
notes: Shown opened out with a fuel tablet on its tray, so it reads as a stove rather than a flat tin; folded it closes to the reference's 147 ml, so the open box is 3.4 times that. The vent cut-outs are painted flush. heating stands for the reference's hotplate quality.

name: Food processor
description: A kitchen motor base under a clear bowl with a chopping blade and a feed tube in the lid. Slices, chops, grinds and mixes. Needs power.
notes: No tool quality: the reference gives none. The blade and spindle inside the bowl show only in game, as the tile draws the clear bowl opaque.

name: Petrol stove
description: A pressure stove that burns petrol: a brass tank with a hand pump, a burner on a riser and three legs carrying a pot ring.
notes: CHECK VOLUME: the box is 4.3 times the reference's 1.25 L, the tank's volume; the open pot stand and the pump and valve key standing out make the bounding box mostly air. heating stands for the reference's hotplate quality.

name: Heat pack
description: A sealed chemical pouch that warms up once its tab is pulled. Heats food or eases a sore muscle, once.
notes: Single use; spent, it becomes the used heat pack, which has its own model.

name: Used heat pack
description: A spent chemical heat pack, cold and gone hard in lumps.
notes: A distinct state of the heat pack with its own model: flatter, grey, lumpy and without its pull tab, so the two read apart on the ground.
